import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set style
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-darkgrid')
sns.set_palette("husl")

# Create figure with subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(18, 12))

# 1. Price distribution by sensor type
ax1 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 1)
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='sensor_type', y='price_usd', order=df.groupby('sensor_type')['price_usd'].median().sort_values().index)
ax1.set_title('Camera Price Distribution by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Sensor Type')
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)')
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 2. Megapixels vs Price with body type
ax2 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 2)
scatter = ax2.scatter(df['megapixels'], df['price_usd'], c=df['model_year'], 
                      cmap='viridis', alpha=0.7, s=df['weight_grams']/20)
ax2.set_title('Megapixels vs Price (colored by year, sized by weight)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Megapixels')
ax2.set_ylabel('Price (USD)')
cbar = plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax2)
cbar.set_label('Model Year')
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 3. Camera count by brand (top 10)
ax3 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 3)
top_brands = df['brand'].value_counts().head(10)
bars = ax3.barh(top_brands.index, top_brands.values)
ax3.set_title('Top 10 Camera Brands by Count', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Number of Cameras')
ax3.invert_yaxis()
for i, (brand, count) in enumerate(top_brands.items()):
    ax3.text(count + 0.5, i, str(count), va='center')
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='x')

# 4. Price trends over years
ax4 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 4)
yearly_stats = df.groupby('model_year').agg({'price_usd': ['mean', 'median', 'count']}).reset_index()
yearly_stats.columns = ['model_year', 'mean_price', 'median_price', 'count']
ax4.plot(yearly_stats['model_year'], yearly_stats['mean_price'], 'o-', linewidth=2, label='Mean Price')
ax4.plot(yearly_stats['model_year'], yearly_stats['median_price'], 's--', linewidth=2, label='Median Price')
ax4.set_title('Camera Price Trends Over Years', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_xlabel('Model Year')
ax4.set_ylabel('Price (USD)')
ax4.legend()
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
ax4.set_xticks(yearly_stats['model_year'][::2])

# 5. 4K video capability by body type
ax5 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 5)
video_data = df.groupby('body_type')['has_video_4k'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)
bars = ax5.bar(video_data.index, video_data.values * 100)
ax5.set_title('Percentage with 4K Video by Body Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_xlabel('Body Type')
ax5.set_ylabel('Percentage with 4K Video (%)')
ax5.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
for i, v in enumerate(video_data.values):
    ax5.text(i, v*100 + 1, f'{v*100:.1f}%', ha='center', va='bottom')
ax5.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# 6. Weight distribution by body type
ax6 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 6)
sns.violinplot(data=df, x='body_type', y='weight_grams', inner='quartile')
ax6.set_title('Camera Weight Distribution by Body Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_xlabel('Body Type')
ax6.set_ylabel('Weight (grams)')
ax6.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax6.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Adjust layout and add overall title
plt.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis: Specifications and Pricing Trends', 
             fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150, facecolor='white')
plt.close()
